settled.why_not_asked: R49-40 already fails any pair where the second sentence corrects the first; the checker's blind spot is a fix to make, not a choice.

settled.point: Swearing
settled.why_not_asked: Each culture's own oaths first, English swears allowed and Earth holy swears out already suit any blend.

settled.point: Foreign words and names on the page
settled.why_not_asked: Romanisation and kept macrons already serve every Eastern register; whether a new word is italicised, glossed or listed in a glossary is asked in VB2.

settled.point: Isaac's characters, their lines and Sodoku's humour
settled.why_not_asked: Every option here governs NPCs and narration; his characters speak, choose and joke as he plays them.

settled.point: Dialogue tags and profanity
settled.why_not_asked: Mostly untagged dialogue, and swearing in mouths and close POV, hold under any blend.

settled.point: Damage numbers, reserve readouts and stat talk inside a fight
settled.why_not_asked: LR11 and LR15 ask them; this section settles only the choreography around the numbers.

settled.point: Named attacks, mid-fight explanation and the watching crowd
settled.why_not_asked: MY4 and MY5 ask mid-fight explanation and the crowd, MY6 the display beats and MY9 the form a name takes; the named attack itself is settled law (R8-24, R50-09).

settled.point: How narration varies a character's epithet inside a scene
settled.why_not_asked: VO4 asks it; NE keeps to sobriquets, hall titles and honorifics.

settled.point: Roving narration across a battlefield
settled.why_not_asked: VO2 asks it; CB7 asks only where a battle's telling lives under whatever POV rule VO2 sets.

settled.point: Idiom banks, sayings in narration, and whether verse appears at all
settled.why_not_asked: DT7 and DT6 ask them; DL3 and DL4 ask only how sayings and verse work in talk.

settled.point: Mimetic and sound words outside explicit scenes
settled.why_not_asked: RH4 asks it; XS1 asks only about explicit scenes.

settled.point: Where figures come from: every number on the page traces to Fracture of Worlds, then the Stat Sheet workbook, then the card.
settled.why_not_asked: Live law and the canon hierarchy. The blend changes how figures show, never their source; LR21 asks only what a readout does with a gap.

settled.point: Readouts print Fracture of Worlds' Stage names (Murmuring, Welling, Splintering), never the cards' older names.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled 2026-09-12; a readout is one more place the ruling applies.

settled.point: Readout text keeps the document rules: timeless wording, the modern-word list and the hard-ban words all apply to it.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled 2026-09-26; a readout is one more in-world text, and every voice LR4 offers is already timeless.

settled.point: Cost always shows in the body, whatever the readouts do.
settled.why_not_asked: This is grimdark's half of the blend and nothing in LitRPG argues against it; LR12 asks only the order of body and number.

settled.point: Readouts never think, decide or speak for your player character, and his figures come from his own card.
settled.why_not_asked: Table law (NATALIE.md and R49-01) that the blend gives no reason to touch.

settled.point: A technique or Trait shown as a card on the page says what it is (mechanism, costs, limits, tell, counters), never how to use it.
settled.why_not_asked: LitRPG skill tooltips already describe effect rather than tactics, so live law fits the genre as written.

settled.point: Item readouts use R46-2's Tier names, Latin forms and Grade bands.
settled.why_not_asked: The ladder was set 2026-09-25; LR17 asks only how it reaches the page.

settled.point: A combat turn is six seconds, so any per-turn readout counts in that unit.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled 2026-09-26 and neutral between the traditions.

settled.point: Your PC Sodoku Moto and the other creators' characters (Haruki, Dova'Kan, Gorgi, Ma'Kovu, Fushigi, Xhem, Sonzai) never carry or receive a comic name, and none of them is renamed.
settled.why_not_asked: A standing table rule in NATALIE.md; Sodoku jokes 'only by accident' (R52-14), and the other creators' names belong to them.

settled.point: No comic name revives a Büri or Mongolian-register form; Moto canon governs every joke near the house.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled 2026-09-12: the Büri register is dead and the sweep of old pages is in progress.

settled.point: Existing names stay as they are; comic names are for new characters, places and things, and Borin Ironheart keeps his name whatever NM8 decides.
settled.why_not_asked: A published name is corrected for grammar only, 'where the name keeps its sound; the rest stays' (R50-02).

settled.point: A comic name that fits no stratum is a legal outlier, and Natalie may build a comic minor NPC as a comic voice from the start.
settled.why_not_asked: Live law ruled 2026-09-26: outliers are 'free, no ratio, no reason needed'. NM1 asks how many you want, which the law leaves open.

settled.point: A foreigner's bent version of a name is spelled as heard in dialogue, and sound-alike names meeting on the page is a beat.
settled.why_not_asked: Live law; NM2 and NM3 build on both.

settled.point: A pun in a foreign tongue uses real, correct words with a true gloss, and an Accord Latin joke is real Latin.
settled.why_not_asked: Live law ruled 2026-09-26; a comic name gets no exemption.

settled.point: Names show romanised only, so no joke may depend on written characters.
settled.why_not_asked: Live law; NM7 asks only which spoken puns the Eastern strata use.

settled.point: No Earth day or month names in any name, and banned modern slang stays out of narration.
settled.why_not_asked: Live vocabulary law; NM2 option C already keeps brand and celebrity puns out.

settled.point: Every comic name still gets a pronunciation line on its card or place page.
settled.why_not_asked: Live law; a joke name is still a name.

settled.point: Epithets in narration, sobriquets, Third Names, hall titles, honorifics and LitRPG titles.
settled.why_not_asked: Asked in VO4 (epithets), NE1 and NE2 (sobriquets, titles, honorifics) and LR18 (titles); this section takes comic names and nicknames only.

settled.point: Earth day and month names never appear, and 'week' becomes the culture's own span.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled 2026-09-26 and already warned by the checker; the blend changes nothing about the calendar.

settled.point: Earth holy swears are replaced by the world's own powers.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled and warned by the checker; VB11 asks only which language a POV may curse in.

settled.point: The short slang and pop-psych lists stay out of narration, and the checker warns on them.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled and checked; gamer words are LR16's, the idiom of thought is IN1's, and VB4 asks how antique narration runs.

settled.point: Collision words (delve, echo, numinous, sovereign, sanctum, weave, ledger) keep only their WOTR sense.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled; no blend choice touches it.

settled.point: Borrowed words are real, correct and romanised, with no kanji or hangul on the page and diacritics kept.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled; every loanword option in this section inherits these conditions.

settled.point: English swears and each culture's own oaths and insults are legal in close-POV narration, the culture's own first.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled 2026-09-26; VB11 asks only whether real Eastern-language swears join them.

settled.point: Real names for borrowed real objects stand where the culture is built on them: a katana is a katana.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled; VB1 asks only about concept words such as qi and the dao.

settled.point: Real science and anatomy terms are exempt from timeless narration and from the modern-word list.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled; VB5 asks how freely narration uses them, never whether they are legal.

settled.point: Technique names and their translations are free in narration, and mechanism terms may stand bare mid-action.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled; MY9 asks what form a technique's name takes on the page.

settled.point: A chant appears in its own language, each practitioner's own.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled; VB3 asks only about learned tags in narration.

settled.point: Old English or Latinate word stock is by ear, the elevated word bank is by ear, and Earth-derived words (herculean, Achilles heel) are legal.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled by ear; VB4 asks how antique the words run, which these rows leave open.

settled.point: Technology and office metaphors appear only where the POV's culture has the thing.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled; it already scales to any culture the blend adds.

settled.point: Seconds and minutes are free in narration.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled; VB6 asks the other units, and clock words feel no blend pressure.

settled.point: In-world documents keep a house style per institution and take the modern-word list.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled; DT9 asks which further forms join them.

settled.point: 'Ozone' and other technical smell words are free; only the stock ozone phrase stays banned.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled in C-090; VB12 extends and trims the ban list without touching it.

settled.point: The repetition tic-word list stays as it is.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled; VB12 handles the separate hard-ban list.

settled.point: Explicit narration stays plain and crude, in working-man anatomical words.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled; the explicit-scene section asks what the blend adds.

settled.point: Whether stat names and figures appear in plain narration.
settled.why_not_asked: LR6 asks it; VB7 sets only how numbers are written and VB8 how terms are capitalised.

settled.point: Which martial vocabulary names the moves in a duel, and the combat checker's word lists.
settled.why_not_asked: CB1 asks the vocabulary and ME2 the checker lists.

settled.point: Honorifics and titles in narration.
settled.why_not_asked: NE2 asks it; VB1 covers only concept words such as qi and the dao.

settled.point: How Draw Age technology looks: the whole Imperial Age span of hardware, rich districts clean and humming, no factory chimneys, the big city Victorian-Edwardian.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled 2026-09-26 and neutral between the strands, and machinery already runs heavy in the archive. LR1 asks what an instrument can show, VB5 how exactly machines are named, and DS5 and DS6 how each culture's eye and buildings bend the look.

settled.point: Sound and smell in description: each culture's sense bank comes first, technical smell words are free, and land and sea keep their own sense order.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled, and every strand works inside it. RH4 asks sound words, SP3 widens openings past the house habit of smell first, and DS6's A adds Temperature to the senses entry.

settled.point: Dress is class-layered, each culture bent by its Inventory.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled 2026-09-26. DS3's B asks whether dress joins the rotation, DS6's B whether each Inventory gains a dress-by-rank field, and DD3 and DD4 who gets a first-sight inventory and in what order.
